NoteRegexAccessor::count¶

Back to Note Regex Accessor API Reference

Signature¶

Note NoteRegexAccessor::count(std::string_view pattern) const

Measure Pattern Frequency Without Extracting Matches¶

count(pattern) compiles pattern as an ECMAScript regular expression and counts its non-overlapping matches independently in every receiver cell. It is the measurement operation in the regex family: use it when the number of occurrences matters but the matching text does not.

The result is an Int64 Note with exactly the receiver’s shape. A cell with no match receives 0; no cell is removed, flattened, or represented by an absent value. This differs from findall, whose variable number of matches requires a ragged TokenBatch, and from Note::count_substring, which treats its argument as literal text rather than regex syntax.

What Counts As A Match¶

Scanning proceeds from left to right. After a match, the next search begins at the end of that match, so results never overlap. For example, aa occurs twice, not three times, in aaaa. Parenthesized capture groups only select subexpressions inside a match; they do not change the count and do not create additional result lanes.

count() has no flags argument. Matching is case-sensitive and uses the default ECMAScript grammar. Use a pattern that expresses the required case behavior, or normalize text before counting. A malformed expression throws pluss::Error before any result is returned.

Type, Shape, And Cost¶

Text and Bytes Notes are accepted. Bool, Int64, Float64, and undefined Notes are rejected because their cells are not character sequences. The regex is compiled once per call and reused for every cell. The method allocates one contiguous Int64 output lane per input cell; it does not allocate or retain the matching substrings. That makes it the direct choice when extraction would only be used to compute a length.

Example 1: Count Every Digit Run Per Cell¶

const auto text = pluss::make_note({"A1,b22,,C333", "none"});
std::cout << pluss::note::print(text.regex().count(R"(\d+)")) << '\n';

Output¶

Note(shape=[2], dim=1, numel=2, dtype=Int64)
[3, 0]

The first cell has three digit runs. Their widths do not matter: 1, 22, and 333 each contribute one match.

Example 2: Higher-Rank Shape Is Preserved¶

const auto grid = pluss::make_note(
    {{"id=7 id=42", "none"}, {"x9", "100 and 200"}});
const auto counts = grid.regex().count(R"(\d+)");
std::cout << "shape=[" << counts.size(0) << ", " << counts.size(1) << "]\n";
std::cout << "values=[";
for (std::size_t i = 0; i < counts.integers().size(); ++i)
  std::cout << (i == 0 ? "" : ", ") << counts.integers()[i];
std::cout << "]\n";

Output¶

shape=[2, 2]
values=[2, 0, 1, 2]

Counting is cellwise, not a reduction over the complete Note. The two-dimensional layout survives unchanged and only each cell’s payload becomes an integer.

Example 3: Matches Do Not Overlap¶

const auto counts =
    pluss::make_note({"aaaa", "id=7 id=42"})
        .regex().count(R"(id=(\d+)|aa)");
std::cout << pluss::note::print(counts) << '\n';

Output¶

Note(shape=[2], dim=1, numel=2, dtype=Int64)
[2, 2]

In aaaa, the first aa consumes positions 0 and 1, and the second consumes positions 2 and 3. In the second cell, the capture group describes the digits inside each id=... match; it does not add separate counts.

Example 4: Invalid Regex Syntax Fails Before Counting¶

try {
  (void)pluss::make_note({"x"}).regex().count("(");
} catch (const pluss::Error& error) {
  const std::string message(error.what());
  std::cout << message.substr(0, message.find('\n')) << '\n';
}

Output¶

regex().count: The expression contained mismatched ( and ).

Example 5: Non-Text Storage Is Rejected¶

try {
  (void)pluss::note::make(std::vector<bool>{true, false})
      .regex().count("true");
} catch (const pluss::Error& error) {
  const std::string message(error.what());
  std::cout << message.substr(0, message.find('\n')) << '\n';
}

Output¶

regex().count: expected Text or Bytes storage

Printed boolean spellings are presentation, not stored text, so the regex engine does not reinterpret them as character data.

See Also¶

  • NoteRegexAccessor::findall: retain each matching substring and its source-cell boundaries.

  • Note::count_substring: count one literal byte sequence without regex metacharacters or compilation.

  • NoteRegexAccessor::search: return one Bool per cell when only presence or absence matters.
